clue.text: Instrument exciting cute rear

indicators.note: exciting means stirring things up, so the letters that follow are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone is aroused by an attractive backside, with an instrument somehow involved.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature is a person used as a tool by another, so an instrument of someone's will.

clue.text: Chestnut horse beset by 100 parasites

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the following words enclose the single letter

parts.note: lice are parasitic insects
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: A chestnut-coloured horse plagued by a hundred parasites.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside LICE, between its C and E. 'Chestnut' looks like the horse's colour but means a stale old joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A chestnut is a stale, overused story or phrase, which is what a cliché is.

clue.text: Old wine unruly adolescent dug out

parts.note: ex means former
cava is Spanish sparkling wine
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a rebellious 1950s British youth

explanation.surface: A wild teenager unearthed a vintage bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Excavated means removed earth from, dug out.

clue.text: Pheasant should be cooked with zero fat in Edgar's book

indicators.note: cooking changes raw ingredients into something new, so these letters are remade

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe in a cookbook by Edgar calls for pheasant cooked without fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zero fat' looks like a diet instruction, but zero is spelt out as four letters of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Rice Burroughs wrote the 1912 novel about the jungle-raised hero.

clue.text: Organ case in fashion around latest pre-Christian time?

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the fashion word wraps the time

parts.note: something in fashion is all the rage
1 BC was the last year before the Christian era, with 1 written as the Roman I

explanation.surface: A fashionable case for a church organ, made in the final years before Christ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the musical instrument, but it is the heart and lungs; the year just before the Christian era is 1 BC.
explanation.definitionFit: The ribcage is the bony frame enclosing the heart and lungs, a case for those organs.

clue.text: Say wife Penny's in pickle

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: to souse is to pickle in brine or vinegar
p is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: Someone notes that their wife is in a mess, along with a girl called Penny.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside SOUSE after its first letter. 'Say' marks wife as only one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wife is one kind of married partner, hence 'Say' to show the example.

clue.text: Healer sat awkwardly with this prophecy

indicators.note: awkwardly means clumsily, so the letters are set out in a jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A faith healer sat uncomfortably through some prediction.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychotherapist treats mental illness through talking, a healer of the mind.

clue.text: Phalanx perhaps holding line in darkness

indicators.note: holding means having inside, so the first word goes round the letter

parts.note: a phalanx is an example of a military unit
l is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A body of troops keeps its formation in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlit has no light, so it lies in darkness.

clue.text: Trainer one in decline that's reversed

indicators.note: reversed means the whole result is turned back to front
one item in another means placed inside it

parts.note: to relapse is to fall back or decline
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sports coach slides into a slump that later turns around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trainer' suggests a coach or a shoe, but it is a frame along which trees are trained.
explanation.definitionFit: An espalier is a trellis on which fruit trees are trained to grow flat against a wall.

clue.text: Look into crash in obstacle race

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the short word is placed within the other

parts.note: a slam is a heavy crash
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Investigators examine a crash during a steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: A slalom is a ski race weaving between gates, a race around obstacles.

clue.text: Suffer at home with worthless mutt

parts.note: being in means being at home
a cur is a mongrel dog of no value

explanation.surface: Someone is stuck in the house with a useless dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to suffer or bring it upon oneself.

clue.text: Corporation to fail — botched entry from board?

parts.note: a corporation is old slang for a paunch
to flop is to fail

explanation.surface: A company is going under, and the clue jokes about a botched entry into the boardroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' and 'board' both pretend to be business words; corporation is a jocular term for a pot belly and the board is a diving board.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive that lands flat on the stomach is a failed, painful entry into the pool from a diving board.

clue.text: Without salt consume the lot — enjoy yourself

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the following words go round the sailor

parts.note: to have all is to consume everything
a salt is a sailor, and an AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A cook or diner told to eat everything unsalted and have fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like seasoning but is an old word for a sailor, and AB is an able seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a ball is an idiom for having a thoroughly good time.

clue.text: Husband books the Spanish lodging-house

parts.note: h is the abbreviation for husband
the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A husband reserves a Spanish guesthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is an establishment providing rooms and lodging for paying guests.

clue.text: Foil lining trays too generously

indicators.note: a lining sits inside, so the letters are found inside the words that follow

parts.note: found running across the end of the first word and into the next two

explanation.surface: Kitchen foil is being used to line baking trays far too lavishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foil' suggests kitchen foil, but it is the comic's foil.
explanation.definitionFit: A stooge is a comedian's straight man, the partner who sets up the jokes, also called a foil.

clue.text: Henri who painted swirling sea mist

indicators.note: swirling suggests things churning about, so the letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A painter named Henri depicted fog rolling over the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was the French artist famous for bold colour and the Fauvist movement.

clue.text: Son is not with mother, left close to bordello in French port

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for son
ain't is the colloquial form of is not
ma is an informal word for mother
l is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: close to here means the close, or end, of the next word

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A son has left his mother's side and gone near a brothel in a French harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint-Malo is a walled port town on the Brittany coast of France.

clue.text: One does not believe it: number soaring in account

indicators.note: being in something means being placed inside it

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account

indicators.note: soaring means rising, and in a down clue rising reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a number is a song in a performance

explanation.surface: A sceptic refuses to credit a figure shooting up in the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' looks like part of the definition but joins SONG before both are turned round; 'number' is a tune, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic holds that God's existence cannot be known, so does not believe either way.

clue.text: Leave 5 in Bow and settle equitably

parts.note: to go is to leave
5 is SPOUSE; in Cockney slang, as spoken in Bow in East London, a wife is 'my old Dutch'

explanation.surface: Someone departs, leaving the 5-across behind, and agrees a fair settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district of East London, home of the Cockney, whose slang 'Dutch' (from duchess) means wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To go Dutch is to split a bill so each party pays an equal or own share.

clue.text: Tom Wolfe at last finding goddess?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, a he-cat

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of the surname

explanation.surface: The novelist Tom Wolfe finally discovers a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Wolfe the American writer splits into a male cat and a last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecate is the Greek goddess of witchcraft, magic and crossroads.

clue.text: Coined money made from tailless breed

indicators.note: without a tail means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a species is a kind or breed

explanation.surface: Coins minted from an animal breed lacking tails, like Manx cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Specie is money in the form of coins rather than paper notes.

clue.text: Showing fibre, criticise Democrat in Congress

indicators.note: in means placed inside the following word

parts.note: congress in the sense of sexual intercourse
to pan is to criticise harshly
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A politician shows backbone by attacking a Democrat in the US Congress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' looks like the US legislature, but it means sexual congress.
explanation.definitionFit: Spandex is a stretchy synthetic fibre used in sportswear.

clue.text: Exam without notes becomes severe test

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the exam word goes round the notes

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
D and E are musical notes

explanation.surface: Sitting an exam without any revision notes is a hard trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without notes' looks like no notes allowed, but 'without' means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful or difficult experience, a severe trial of endurance.

clue.text: Hold forth over level of tax?

parts.note: o is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over
a tax rate is the level at which tax is charged

explanation.surface: Someone lectures at length about how high taxes are.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak pompously or at length, to hold forth.

clue.text: Delight in morning milk

parts.note: a.m. denotes the morning
to milk is to exploit or use

explanation.surface: Someone takes pleasure in the morning milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'milk' looks like a drink, but it is the verb meaning to exploit.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse is to entertain or delight someone.

clue.text: Unusual fish from rare catch distributed

indicators.note: distributed means spread about, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An angler shares out an exotic fish landed in an unusual haul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual fish' reads like a species, but 'fish' is the slang for a person, as in 'a queer fish'.
explanation.definitionFit: A character is an eccentric individual, just as an odd fish is a strange person.

clue.text: Loudly extolled as Orangeman with French media boss?

parts.note: Donald Trump, jokingly an orange man for his complexion
et is French for and, which means with
ed is short for editor

explanation.surface: Something was praised to the skies as if by an Ulster Protestant alongside a French newspaper chief.
explanation.walkthrough: An Orangeman is a member of the Protestant Orange Order in Northern Ireland; here it is twisted to mean Trump.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet something is to proclaim or praise it noisily.

clue.text: Firm haggles periodically for representation

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the even-placed letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A company bargains now and then over how it is portrayed.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a likeness or depiction of something.

clue.text: Native American concealing a small wrinkle

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the outer word goes round the rest

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
taken as written
s is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A Native American hides a minor complication.
explanation.definitionFit: A crease is a line or fold in skin or cloth, a wrinkle.

clue.text: Parrot after flight giving way-out assessment?

parts.note: a flight is an escape or departure
Poll is a traditional name for a parrot

explanation.surface: A parrot that has flown off provides an outlandish judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: The parrot comes after the flight in the answer. 'Way-out' means bizarre in the surface but is a pun on voters on their way out of the polling station.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit poll surveys voters as they leave the polling station, assessing them on their way out.
